ecommerce_revenue.text:
Description: In 2024, online sales accounted for nine percent of all retail sales in Brazil. This represents an increase of almost three percentage points compared to 2019. Even though e-commerce had gained ground in the Brazilian retail market before 2020, the
COVID-19 pandemic accelerated this trend. Read more
Note(s): Brazil; 2019 to 2025*; * 2025 forecast. The release date is that of last access. Read more
Source(s): Associação Brasileira de Comércio Eletrônico

Description: In 2025, e-commerce in Brazil generated around 235.5 billion Brazilian reals in revenue, marking a 15.3 percent increase from the previous year's total of approximately 204.3 billion. The online shopping sector experienced significant growth in 2020,
driven by the COVID-19 pandemic, with revenues expanding by 40 percent. Read more
Note(s): Brazil; 2019 to 2025
Source(s): Associação Brasileira de Comércio Eletrônico

categories.text:
Description: In the first half of 2024, the home appliances sector accounted for almost 40 percent of the Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV) in Brazil. Health was the second most important e-commerce category based on GMV share, with about 20 percent, not
considering the other categories. Based on the number of orders, fragrances and cosmetics was the best-selling segment. Read more
Note(s): H1 2024
Source(s): Ebit; NielsenIQ

forecast_users.text:
Description: The number of users in the e-commerce market in Brazil was modeled to stand at 128.3 million users in 2024. Following a continuous upward trend, the number of users has risen by 74.58 million users since 2017. Between 2024 and 2029, the number of
users will rise by 49.38 million users, continuing its consistent upward trajectory. Read more
Note(s): Brazil; 2017 to 2029
Source(s): Statista; Statista Market Insights
